Reforming the Mechanism: Editing Reasoni.title: Reforming the Mechanism: Editing Reasoning Patterns in LLMs with Circuit Reshaping
Reforming the Mechanism: Editing Reasoni.abstract: Large language models can make systematic, pattern-specific reasoning mistakes, and broad training fixes are inefficient and often disrupt other abilities. This paper introduces Reasoning Editing, targeted edits to a specific reasoning pattern, highlighting a key trade-off between generality and locality. To reduce this trade-off, we propose REdit, which reshapes underlying reasoning circuits to limit interference before applying a lightweight edit.

BrainTAP: Brain Disorder Prediction with.title: BrainTAP: Brain Disorder Prediction with Adaptive Distill and Selective Prior Integration
BrainTAP: Brain Disorder Prediction with.abstract: This paper introduces BrainTAP, a transformer-based framework for brain disorder prediction that integrates functional and structural connectivity while preserving their heterogeneous properties. The model employs adaptive mutual distillation to enable controlled cross-modal interaction and selectively incorporates expert-defined neurobiological priors through learnable gates and personalized attention mechanisms, improving both representation quality and interpretability.

MolEdit: Knowledge Editing for Multimoda.title: MolEdit: Knowledge Editing for Multimodal Molecule Language Models
MolEdit: Knowledge Editing for Multimoda.abstract: MolEdit is a framework for precisely editing facts inside multimodal molecule language models so they can fix outdated or wrong chemistry and biomedical knowledge without retraining. It uses a Multi-Expert Knowledge Adapter to edit specific facets such as functional groups and properties, plus an Expert-Aware Editing Switcher to trigger edits only on closely matching inputs, and MEBench to evaluate reliability, locality, and generality, showing sizable gains over prior editors.

Learning from Diverse Reasoning Paths wi.title: Learning from Diverse Reasoning Paths with Routing and Collaboration
Learning from Diverse Reasoning Paths wi.abstract: This work proposes QR-Distill, a distillation framework that filters for correct, LLM-judged high-quality chains-of-thought, conditionally routes the remaining paths to students based on their current state, and enables mutual student collaboration via feature-level peer teaching. Across multiple reasoning datasets, it outperforms single- and multi-path baselines.

ST-FiT: Inductive Spatial-Temporal Forec.title: ST-FiT: Inductive Spatial-Temporal Forecasting with Limited Training Data
ST-FiT: Inductive Spatial-Temporal Forec.abstract: This paper studies an under-explored problem of inductive forecasting with limited training data, which requires models to generalize learned spatial-temporal dependencies from nodes with available training data to nodes without. We propose ST-FiT, which achieves superior performance without additional fine-tuning.

BrainMAP: Learning Multiple Activation P.title: BrainMAP: Learning Multiple Activation Pathways in Brain Networks
BrainMAP: Learning Multiple Activation P.abstract: While significant progress has been made in understanding brain activity through functional connectivity graphs, challenges remain in capturing the complex, long-range dependencies and multiple pathways inherent in these graphs. We introduce BrainMAP, which extracts multiple long-range activation pathways with adaptive sequentialization and pathway aggregation.

BIC: Twitter Bot Detection with Text-Gra.title: BIC: Twitter Bot Detection with Text-Graph Interaction and Semantic Consistency
BIC: Twitter Bot Detection with Text-Gra.abstract: We propose BIC, a bot-detection model that interacts and exchanges information across text modality and graph modality via a text-graph interaction module. BIC contains a semantic consistency module that derives inconsistency from tweets via attention weights to identify advanced bots.
